catalog_quote: Alone among reported Persian dialects they have an unstressed modal prefix be- to mark the present indicative and past continuous, as in bebīnom “I see,” bedīdom “I used to see.” ... Verbs based on the present stem are stressed on the personal endings; verbs based on the past stem are stressed on the last syllable of the stem, as in begoróm, “I take,” goróftom “I took,” bego-róftom “I was taking.” In compound verbs the incorporated nominal constituent is stressed. ... When preceded by the negative prefix, stressed na-, the -b is nasalized, as in Dezfūlī and Šūštarī namḵerom “I don’t buy.” A handful of verbs take unstressed forms of me- as prefix ... The past endings are enclitic and are identical with present-tense forms of “to be.” ... as in Šūštarī varsādám, varsādē´ “I am standing, you are standing” (< varsada + -m, -i). ... The imperative is negated by the stressed prefix má-. ... In both dialects there is also a contrastive suffix, stressed -ka, ... as in doḵtarka mord “the girl ... died.” Both also have a deictive suffix, stressed -(h)a ... || [KHUZESTAN viii, Morphology:] The principal noun markers are suffixes: (1) plural: Baḵt., D-Š stressed –(h)ā, –un ...; (2) definite object: Baḵt., D-Š unstressed -(n)a ...; (3) eżāfa: unstressed –e, as in Persian; (4) the so-called “indefinite article”: unstressed –i, –ē, as in Persian; (5) the antecedent of a relative clause: unstressed –i, –ē as in Persian; (6) contrast: stressed Baḵt. –(i)ka, D-Š –(a)ka

new_statements.rule_in_words: Persian-type morphologically governed rightmost stress: in present-stem verb forms stress falls on the personal ending (word-final: be-gor-óm), in past-stem forms on the final syllable of the stem (goróft-om); the indicative prefix be- and me- are unstressed while negative na- and prohibitive má- attract stress; in nouns the plural suffix -(h)ā/-un and contrastive -(a)ka / deictic -(h)a are stressed, whereas the object marker -(n)a, ezafe -e and indefinite/relative -i/-ē are unstressed enclitics — i.e. stress on the last syllable of the nominal word excluding enclitics. The article never states the rule for bare noun stems in one sentence; final stress there is inferred from the stressed-suffix/unstressed-enclitic pattern and MacKinnon's explicit comparison with colloquial Persian.
new_statements.exceptions: Unstressed be-/me- prefixes; stressed na-, má-; compound verbs stress the incorporated nominal; counterfactual suffix -ē unstressed; a few verbs (dārom, dunom, tarom) take no prefix.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements are morpheme-by-morpheme (word-level, citation forms with acute accents on examples), covering both Dezfuli and Shushtari jointly; no phrase-level discussion. A general phonological statement of word stress is expected only in MacKinnon 1974 (not accessible).
new_statements.identity_note: Both EIr articles treat Dezfuli and Shushtari together ('D-Š'), matching Glottolog's language-level dezf1238 Dezfuli-Shushtari; the stress statements are given as holding for both varieties. Glottolog's ref 'Moqaddam 1929, O dialekt g. Shustera' is the same item that MacKinnon's bibliography attributes to B. V. Miller (Iran III, Leningrad 1929).

sources.note: Phonology section covers vowels/consonants/processes only; stress statements are in Morphology: unstressed modal prefix be-; present-stem verbs stressed on the personal ending, past-stem verbs on the last stem syllable (begoróm, goróftom, bego-róftom); incorporated nominal of compound verbs stressed; negative na- and prohibitive má- stressed; unstressed me-; contrastive -ka and deictic -(h)a stressed; counterfactual -ē unstressed. No explicit sentence on stress in uninflected nouns.

sources.note: For Dezfuli-Šuštari (D-Š) and Bakhtiari noun markers: plural -(h)ā, -un stressed; definite-object -(n)a unstressed; ezafe -e unstressed; indefinite -i/-ē unstressed; relative antecedent -i/-ē unstressed; contrastive D-Š -(a)ka stressed. Says D-Š is the only Khuzestan dialect described in detail (MacKinnon 1974).
